title: Day 3
text: I have stopped watching for a sail. Strike one stone hard against another and it flakes off an edge. An edge lashed to a stick with a vine is a knife, and a knife gives everything else: bait from a fish, and a bone for a better hook.

title: Day 9
text: The little striped thieves strip my hook all day, and I never see them do it. A disc of coconut shell threaded on a cord rides on the water above the bait: when it dips, strike. After dark the red ones with the great eyes come out of the rock and take a sand flea boldly.

title: Day 14
text: The good fish lie where the rock drops away into blue water, and a bare bait never gets there. A pebble with a groove ground round it, tied above the hook, carries the bait out and takes it down to them.

title: Day 20
text: Behind the reef there is a lagoon as clear as air. The grey ghosts come onto the flats with their tails in the air, rooting for crabs and fleas. Drop the bait well ahead of them and let them find it. Put it on their heads and they are gone like smoke.

title: Day 27
text: Bamboo grows behind the palms where the ground is wet. A long cane throws nearly twice as far as the ship’s rod, out past the reef edge, and it bends where the old rod would break. Twice I have seen grey backs rolling out there: dolphins, hunting together.

title: Day 33
text: Some fish want nothing dead. The blue-backed jacks at the reef edge follow a bait and turn away. A tuft of gull feather on a flash of shell, drawn back in steady pulses, they hit like a thrown stone. So does the long toothed one that hangs off the edge.

title: Day 41
text: Split cane packed with coconut husk and lit at the fire burns for an hour. The night water is another country: red-eyed fish, things walking on the bottom, eyes in every crack. And at dusk something red and heavy takes cut fish at the reef edge and goes straight down.

title: Day 52
text: Wove a basket trap from fronds on a cane frame. Left overnight by the rocks with fish scraps in it, it held a whiskered lobster by morning. Once it held nothing but crab shells and a smear of ink. The round silver ones with the sickle fins will look at little but a crab.

title: Day 60
text: Fish split and hung over a slow fire keeps for weeks. I will need it. A fish bone ground to a point and pierced sews woven fronds into a sail. At first light great silver fish roll in the lagoon channel, gulping air like men. One took my feather and I never turned it. Not with this gear. Not on this island.

title: Day 71
text: The raft is lashed. From the point at sunset I took a bearing on the smoke that rises some evenings to the west-south-west: a port, two days' sail if the wind holds. Whoever finds this: a hull, a mast, a sail, an oar to steer, food for the crossing. Then go.
